summary: Jazz (small-combo swing): 100-160 BPM, a swung ride with the hi-hat on 2 and 4, an upright bass walking quarter notes through ii-V-I changes, a piano comping rootless 7th/9th voicings, a vibraphone or horn on the melody; knowledge/style/jazz.json is its template
body: Tempo: medium swing 110-160 BPM (cool jazz 110-160, hard bop 120-200, bebop faster); swing ratio about 60-67%, never grid-straight.

Drums: the ride carries the time (ding, ding-a-ding, swung), the hi-hat closed with the foot on 2 and 4, the snare only comping and the kick feathered or sparse; brushes for ballads; soft, natural, a jazz kit, not punchy or processed.

Bass: an upright (acoustic) bass walking quarter notes through the changes, chord tones on the beats and chromatic approach notes, the root on each new chord; a 2-feel (half notes) for a calmer section; louder in the mix than in pop, never high-passed hard.

Harmony: 7th, 9th and 13th chords, never plain triads; ii-V-I, I-vi-ii-V turnarounds, tritone substitutions; a grand piano comping in the middle register in short, varied rhythms, rootless voicings (3rd and 7th, the bass has the root).
Lead: the head on a horn (alto or tenor sax, trumpet, muted trumpet) or a vibraphone, call-and-response phrasing; the template uses the vibraphone, clear and soft.
Texture/master: transparent and acoustic: a small room, light compression at most (2-4 dB on the bus), dynamics kept (about -18 to -14 LUFS); no saturation, sidechain or bright EQ.

Sources (2026-11-26): MusicProductionWiki 'How to make jazz music'; MusicRadar 'How to program a basic jazz comp rhythm using a software drum kit'; Learn Jazz Standards 'Ultimate Jazz Comping 101'; Marshall University 'Rhythm section roles in standard swing'.
Apply: pattern/gmd-jazz-beat-1 on the drums, then pattern/jazz-ii-v-i on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/jazz.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
